newsitem.title: IRAQ: Kurdish faction denies attack on rivals' city.
newsitem.headline: Kurdish faction denies attack on rivals' city.

text.p: Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) guerrillas, already holding the northern Iraqi capital of Arbil, said they had made no move to attack the city of Sulaimaniya, their rivals' last remaining stronghold.
"The KDP has no plans to take Sulaimaniya," Sami Abderrahman, a KDP leader, told reporters late on Monday. Such reports, he said, were "a ploy" by the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK).
Abderrahman blamed the PUK for cutting water and electricity into Arbil -- under PUK control until combined Iraqi national and KDP irregular forces threw them out at the weekend.
He said renewed fighting was likely unless utilities were restored to the city of one million.
"If they continue to cut the electricity and to punish the people of Arbil and the KDP tries to ... secure electricity and water for Arbil, then the KDP should not be blamed.
"We are in a state of armed conflict" with the PUK, he said, briefing reporters in the nearby city of Salahuddin. Journalists have been barred by the KDP from approaching Arbil.

Earlier, the United States said that Iraqi troops appeared to be moving deeper into Kurdish opposition-held territory in northern Iraq, and President Bill Clinton had prepared a "course of action" in response.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry, speaking with reporters as the president campaigned in Wisconsin, said there was evidence that some of the Iraqi forces that overran Arbil during the weekend were "penetrating deeper" into northern Iraq.
He said the military advance threatened Sulaimaniya.
